text:
A: Hi! Hello, can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah, hi, I can hear you fine. I'm Daniel.
A: Chiara. Nice to meet you! Sorry, I always feel like I'm shouting on these.
B: No, you're fine. Where are you based?
A: Fulham, so west London, by the New King's Road. And you?
B: Worthing. On the coast, West Sussex.
A: Oh, the seaside! That's so nice. Erm, I'm from Turin originally, so I'm always a bit jealous of people with the sea. Does that make sense, being jealous of Worthing?
B: [laughs] Not many people say that. It's windy, mostly. So what do you do?
A: So, erm, I was in brand partnerships for a luxury accessories house here in London. Hotels, influencers, collaborations, that kind of thing. And now I'm sort of... consulting. Freelance strategy work, for a candle brand at the moment. Taking a little break to think about the next step, to be honest.
B: Right. That sounds like quite a big world.
A: It's, yeah, it's a lot of lunches. Cioè, it's work, but it's a lot of lunches. What about you?
B: What do I do? Erm, I run the trade counter at a builders' merchant in Lancing. So plasterers, chippies, people coming in at half six wanting timber and plasterboard. Quotes, stock queries. Not very glamorous.
A: No, but that's so useful! Literally, everybody needs that. My husband and I can't even put up a shelf.
B: You'd be surprised how many builders can't either.
A: [laughs]
B: I'm also doing an Open University course in the evenings. Social history. Slowly.
A: Oh, that's amazing. I think I saw the books behind you, in the photo? I remember thinking, okay, he reads.
B: Yeah, that's them. It's sort of something I never finished, so.
A: Sorry, never finished?
B: I started a degree and left after the first year. Money, mainly. So this is me having another go.
A: I think that's really brave, honestly.
B: Thanks. What's the best thing about London for you, after Turin?
A: Erm, the galleries, the restaurants. I finally got a table at this place in Soho everyone is talking about, it took me three weeks. But the Italian food here, to be honest... no. Carbonara with cream. I can't.
B: [laughs] I think I'm guilty of that. My mum's version has peas in it.
A: Peas! No. Okay, I forgive your mum.
B: Do you cook, then?
A: Yes, every Sunday I make my nonna's agnolotti, by hand. It takes the whole afternoon. Tom, my husband, he's at a law firm in the City and he's very late every night, so Sunday is when we actually eat together. Is that what you mean?
B: Yeah, that sounds really nice. I do the dinners at home on Thursdays and Sundays. I'm working through a Middle Eastern cookbook at the minute. Did a lamb thing with pomegranate last week that sort of worked.
A: Sort of worked! That's how cooking is, no? Did your parents like it?
B: My dad asked if there was any gravy.
A: [laughs] Oh my God. That's my father with anything that isn't Italian.
B: Do you travel much? I did a week in Porto last year.
A: I love Lisbon! We did Lisbon, a little boutique hotel in Alfama. Porto I haven't done. Is it worth it?
B: Yeah, I'd say so. It's cheaper than Lisbon, and the river's—
